hook.line: Every deal has a catch: "I'll sign, as long as they let us stay." Conditions like this are how you bargain and how you protect yourself, and Tomás is about to need them at the hearing.
hook.es: Firmo con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos.
hook.en: I'll sign as long as they let us stay.

examples.es: Firmo con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos.
examples.en: I'll sign as long as they let us stay.

examples.es: Te llamo en caso de que haya algún problema.
examples.en: I'll call you in case there's a problem. (to a friend)

examples.es: Te presto el carro con tal de que lo cuides.
examples.en: I'll lend you the car as long as you take care of it. (to a friend)

examples.es: En caso de que llueva, la reunión es adentro.
examples.en: In case it rains, the meeting is inside.

examples.es: Vale viene con tal de que no sea muy tarde.
examples.en: Vale is coming as long as it isn't too late.

examples.es: Cierro con llave en caso de que alguien entre.
examples.en: I lock up in case someone comes in.

rule:
Some little phrases set a condition or a precaution:
*con tal de que*: as long as, provided that
*en caso de que*: in case
*a menos que*: unless
*siempre que*: as long as

The verb right after them takes the "wish" form: *dejen*, *haya*, *cuides*, *llueva*, *sea*. The thing is only a possibility, not a fact yet. English leaves the verb alone ("as long as it isn't late"), but Spanish marks it.

Compare plain *si*: *Firmo si me dan una copia* keeps the ordinary verb. With these four phrases, use the wish form, and never *-ría*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these connectors conditional conjunctions. They always take the subjunctive.

readAndPick.es: Firmo con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos.
options: I'll sign as long as they let us stay.
I'll sign in case they let us stay.
I'll sign because they let us stay.

readAndPick.es: Te llamo en caso de que haya algún problema.
options: I'll call you as long as there's a problem.
I called you because there was a problem.
I'll call you in case there's a problem.

readAndPick.es: Te presto el carro con tal de que lo cuides.
options: I'll lend you the car in case you take care of it.
I'll lend you the car as long as you take care of it.
I lend you the car because you take care of it.

readAndPick.es: En caso de que llueva, la reunión es adentro.
options: In case it rains, the meeting is inside.
Since it rained, the meeting is inside.
As long as it rains, the meeting is inside.

readAndPick.es: Vale viene con tal de que no sea muy tarde.
options: Vale is coming in case it isn't too late.
Vale is coming as long as it isn't too late.
Vale is coming because it isn't too late.

readAndPick.es: Cierro con llave en caso de que alguien entre.
options: I lock up because someone came in.
I lock up as long as someone comes in.
I lock up in case someone comes in.

readAndPick.es: Firmo si me dan una copia.
options: I'll sign if they give me a copy.
I'll sign in case they give me a copy.

readAndPick.es: Ustedes pueden quedarse con tal de que no hagan ruido.
options: You all stayed because you didn't make noise.
You all can stay as long as you don't make noise.
You all can stay in case you don't make noise.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right verb and type the whole sentence: *Te presto el carro con tal de que lo ___.* (*cuides* or *cuidas*)
yourTurn.answer: Te presto el carro con tal de que lo cuides.
yourTurn.why: After *con tal de que*, the verb takes the wish form: *cuides*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I'll call you in case there's a problem.
yourTurn.answer: Te llamo en caso de que haya algún problema.
accept: En caso de que haya algún problema, te llamo.
yourTurn.why: *En caso de que* is "in case", and *haya* is the wish form of *hay*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'll sign as long as they let us stay.
yourTurn.answer: Firmo con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos.
accept: Con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos, firmo.
yourTurn.why: *Con tal de que* means "as long as"; *dejen* is the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: In case it rains, the meeting is inside.
yourTurn.answer: En caso de que llueva, la reunión es adentro.
accept: La reunión es adentro en caso de que llueva.
yourTurn.why: The connector comes first, then the wish form *llueva*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Vale is coming as long as it isn't too late.
yourTurn.answer: Vale viene con tal de que no sea muy tarde.

yourTurn.prompt: Change the idea: *Cierro con llave.* Say: I lock up in case someone comes in.
yourTurn.answer: Cierro con llave en caso de que alguien entre.
yourTurn.why: Add *en caso de que* and the wish form *entre*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a group: *Puedes quedarte con tal de que no hagas ruido.* Say: You all can stay as long as you don't make noise.
yourTurn.answer: Ustedes pueden quedarse con tal de que no hagan ruido.
accept: Pueden quedarse con tal de que no hagan ruido.
yourTurn.why: Switch to *ustedes*: *pueden* and the wish form *hagan*.

pitfalls.wrong: Firmo con tal de que nos dejan quedarnos.
pitfalls.right: Firmo con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *con tal de que* the verb takes the wish form: *dejen*, not *dejan*.

pitfalls.wrong: En caso de que llovería, la reunión es adentro.
pitfalls.right: En caso de que llueva, la reunión es adentro.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Do not use *-ría* here: after *en caso de que* use the wish form, *llueva*.

pitfalls.wrong: Firmo con tal de nos dejen quedarnos.
pitfalls.right: Firmo con tal de que nos dejen quedarnos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The connector is the whole phrase *con tal de que*, so keep the *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Te llamo en caso de que hay algún problema.
pitfalls.right: Te llamo en caso de que haya algún problema.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Hay* is the plain form; after *en caso de que* you need the wish form, *haya*.

personal: Set a condition for something you would agree to, starting with *Voy con tal de que…*, or a precaution starting with *Llevo… en caso de que…*
